summary: AISDLC-487: main branch-protection posture — strict-up-to-date + no merge-queue causes merge starvation under parallel/autonomous dispatch

options.description: Re-introduce a GitHub merge queue — PRs serialize + auto-rebase, no up-to-date race. Cost: queue latency. (Was dropped in AISDLC-400.)
Set strict=false (drop require-up-to-date) — PRs merge without rebasing onto every intervening landing. Cost: cross-PR merge-skew risk (the AISDLC-406 main-health-monitor backstops it).
Keep strict=true but add robust auto-rebase+re-sign automation so the race self-heals without operator intervention. Cost: still re-runs full CI per rebase.

rationale: Root cause is require-up-to-date (strict=true), not the absent queue: strict=true forces a rebase of every other open PR on each landing (O(N^2) rebase+CI+re-sign). merge-queue serializes (opposite of concurrent disjoint merges) + full CI per entry; auto-rebase is the status quo that re-staled #828. strict-false composes with AISDLC-491 (patch-scoped verifier = attestation rebase-invariant for disjoint PRs): #491 removes attestation invalidation, strict-false removes the forced rebase = concurrent disjoint merges. Merge-skew backstopped by AISDLC-406 main-health-monitor (full suite per push, P0 issue). Caveat: [main-health] issues become load-bearing P0.

summary: Relax v6 attestation subject.sha1 head-binding when patch-id + Merkle root + trusted signature already verify (eliminate orphan-subject CI failures)

options.description: Drop the subject.sha1 reachability requirement when content patch-id matches the envelope filename AND the Merkle root verifies AND the signature is from a trusted key — content is already bound by patch-id (in-toto/SLSA-style). Eliminates the orphan-after-rebase CI-vs-local asymmetry.

Keep subject.sha1 head-binding as-is; rely on the tactical pre-push guard (re-sign reachable subject) to prevent orphan subjects. Lower change surface, retains belt-and-suspenders commit binding, but the local-passes/CI-fails fragility remains latent.
Keep binding but have CI deep-fetch/unshallow so the subject is reachable. Rejected on examination — orphaned (rebased-away) commits are unreferenced and not fetchable by SHA.

body: Root cause: PR #912 (AISDLC-538) failed the CI attestation gate because subject.sha1 pointed at an orphaned pre-rebase commit unreachable in CI's shallow clone; the AISDLC-448 tree-equivalence relaxation works locally (orphan in object store) but not CI -> local-passes/CI-fails. The patch-id (envelope filename) already content-binds the envelope to the exact diff, so subject.sha1 is largely redundant with patch-id+Merkle+signature. Security note: an envelope signed for diff-X's patch-id cannot validate diff-Y (different patch-id -> different filename -> not found); cross-PR reuse requires byte-identical diffs (benign). Tracked alongside the tactical guard task. Routed to operator (Engineering/Security) since it changes the attestation trust model.

rationale: Operator decision 2026-06-13: relax. patch-id (envelope filename, from diff content) already content-binds the envelope; Merkle root + trusted-key signature authenticate reviewer evidence; subject.sha1 commit-binding is redundant and the sole source of the orphan-after-rebase CI fragility (4 recovery re-signs in the 2026-06-12 drain, incl PR #912). In-toto/SLSA/Sigstore bind to content digests not commit SHAs. Replay counter-argument answered: cross-PR reuse needs a byte-identical diff = same patch-id = same review (benign). Impl: verifier accepts when content-patch-id==filename + Merkle verifies + trusted signature, WITHOUT subject.sha1 reachability. AISDLC-545 becomes belt-and-suspenders; fold relaxation into AISDLC-543.

taskId: AISDLC-570
sourceWorktree: /Users/dominique/Documents/dev/ai-sdlc/ai-sdlc/.worktrees/aisdlc-570

AISDLC-570 opt-a feasibility investigation (docs/design/aisdlc-570-opt-a-feasibility.md in this PR). Claude Code CONFIRMED feasible (per-subagent harness transcript at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, verified live on this machine). Codex: Claude-side wrapper transcript feasible; native codex exec double-binding unverified; bare --spawner codex unverified. Copilot: no evidence of a subagent-transcript artifact found. Core architectural fork: binding the leaf's harnessTranscriptHash to the harness transcript can only be independently re-verified by a downstream CI verifier if the transcript itself is committed (RFC-0042 currently keeps transcripts gitignored, local-disk, 90-day retention) OR the check stays sign-time-only (smaller security uplift, and only closes the adversarial-coordinator threat, not an adversarial-operator threat). This departs from v6's core 'CI can independently verify without any local-machine-only artifact' design property and needs operator routing before any schema/verifier code is written.

rationale: opt-a's target is the adversarial COORDINATOR (an automated process that self-authors instead of spawning a reviewer), NOT the operator — RFC-0042 trusts the operator's ed25519 key (Q3/AISDLC-140 audit-at-source). Bind an additive harnessTranscriptHash into the leaf, verified ONCE at sign time when the ephemeral ~/.claude transcript exists; informational to CI. Matches in-toto/SLSA/Sigstore (trust the signer's provenance claim, not CI re-derivation). Rejected opt2 (commit transcripts): defends the out-of-scope malicious-operator threat at the cost of reversing RFC-0042's deliberate transcript-privacy/gitignore design. Rejected opt3 (operator-local spot-check): binding into the signed Merkle-rooted leaf is tamper-evident and auditable, an out-of-band manual check is not. Composes with AISDLC-572 role-binding; implement under AISDLC-570.

summary: Should ai-sdlc init install a default enforcement mechanism for review attestation, or stay audit-only (adopter-owned) by design?

options.description: Add a default hard-blocking CI check (or install --with-branch-protection's required-approving-review by default) so a freshly initialized repo cannot merge code without at least one review signal. Cost: installing CI/branch-protection into an adopter's repo is intrusive and reverses the framework's own Q3 design decision (docs/operations/quality-gate.md: 'audit at source, enforce at deploy'; attestation is audit-only even in ai-sdlc's own repo, where governance is enforced by an operator reviewing status, not branch protection).

Keep audit-only as the default (status quo), rely on the new 'ai-sdlc doctor' command (shipped in this PR) plus stronger generated-file/init-output disclosure (also shipped in this PR) to make the gap instantly discoverable instead of silent. Cost: an adopter who never runs 'ai-sdlc doctor' or reads the disclosure can still merge 200+ PRs with zero review, same as the reported incident — the fix is discoverability, not prevention.

Make init prompt explicitly ask 'do you want this to be enforced (blocking) or audit-only?' when attestation + branch-protection are both selected, defaulting the interactive prompt to enforced=true while keeping --yes/CI default at audit-only for backward compat. Middle ground between a and b; adds wizard complexity and a second branch-protection-application code path (required_pull_request_reviews with require_code_owner_reviews or a stricter minimum) that would need its own design + soak window.

summary: AISDLC-673 handover: may another executor finish delta's work (head 6dafd29f7) while delta is out until Oct 6?

options.description: Hand over now from committed head 6dafd29f7, fresh reviewer spawn, rebase+sign+push, record handover
Wait for delta to return on 2026-10-06
Re-do 673 from scratch in a new worktree

body:
## Problem
AISDLC-673 (local head 6dafd29f7, 126 tests passing) has only the test re-review, rebase and sign left. Its owner, executor delta, is unavailable until 2026-10-06. 673 gates 672, 675 and 676, which is the RFC-0052 staged-review critical path. operator-dispatch asked the planner whether alpha or gamma may take it over from delta's worktree.

## Prior art / research
- RFC-0051 §authority matrix: the dispatch tier owns throughput; a durable assignment channel exists so assignments survive an executor being gone.
- RFC-0042/0046: the remaining steps are mechanical; the one trust-sensitive step (reviewer verdicts) must be produced by a fresh reviewer spawn, never copied from another session.
- Earlier same-night call: 681 was NOT handed over, because it was mid-push (a half-pushed branch is not a clean handover point). That call was specific, not a rule.

## Options
- **opt-a (recommended): hand over now, with conditions.** Start from the committed head only; fresh reviewer spawn for the re-review; rebase, rebuild, v6 sign, push; record the handover in the brief and PR body. Pro: critical path keeps moving tonight; no trust shortcut. Con: a second executor spends ~1 task-slot on work it did not author.
- **opt-b: wait for delta (Oct 6).** Pro: single author per task. Con: 4-day stall on 672/675/676 and the RFC-0052 chain; the operator's standing rule is cost-of-waiting > cost-of-wrong-decision.
- **opt-c: dispatch re-does 673 from scratch in a new worktree.** Pro: no shared-worktree ambiguity. Con: throws away 126 passing tests and a day of work; strictly worse than opt-a.

## Counter-argument to the recommendation
If 673's committed head has unresolved review findings the handover executor cannot see, it may ship something delta intended to rework. Mitigation: the fresh reviewer spawn is exactly the check that catches that.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Recommended option taken per operator's standing instruction (run rubric, pick recommendation, catalog for morning review). Communicated to operator-dispatch 2026-10-03 ~05:30Z with the four conditions. Operator may override via cli-decisions override DEC-0015 <opt>.

summary: Landing order for AISDLC-656.1 (signed, head 5b1f6ec3) vs AISDLC-653.2, which edit the same replay files for repoId

options.description: 656.1 pushes as is; 653.2 rebases on it and trims scope to the uncovered remainder
653.2 lands first; 656.1 rebases and takes a fresh review round
Fold 653.2 items 1-3 into 656.1; mark 653.2 reduced or done by it

body:
## Problem
alpha's 656.1 branch (signed locally, head 5b1f6ec3, based on aeb22661, not pushed) already threads repoId through replay-run.ts, replay-commands.ts and replay-report.ts. Task 653.2 (replay-run records carry repoId; dep 653.1 merged; must precede 656.2) has scope items 1-3 in the same files. Whichever lands second conflicts and may be partly redundant. 653.2 is unclaimed (DoR not done).

## Prior art
- Standing rule: signed, review-complete work is not re-reviewed for ordering reasons alone; a patch-id change forces a fresh review round (RFC-0042 patch-scoped verifier).
- One task per PR; scope trimming of an unclaimed task against already-landed work is a mechanical DoR step, not a design change.

## Options
- **opt-a (recommended):** 656.1 pushes now as is. 653.2 rebases on it when claimed and trims scope to what 656.1 did not cover; if nothing remains of items 1-3, the task body records "items 1-3 landed in 656.1" and keeps only the rest. Pro: zero cost tonight, no re-review, preserves 653.2 as the audit point for 656.2's dependency. Con: 653.2's DoR must verify the overlap honestly.
- **opt-b:** 653.2 first, then 656.1 rebases and re-reviews. Pro: tasks land in numeric dependency order. Con: throws away a signed review on finished work for an ordering that nothing depends on.
- **opt-c:** fold 653.2 items 1-3 into 656.1 and mark 653.2 reduced/done. Pro: fewest PRs. Con: changes 656.1's reviewed scope after sign (re-review anyway), and 656.2's dependency on 653.2 then points at a task that was partly closed by a different PR; muddier audit trail.

## Counter-argument
If 653.2's items 1-3 differ semantically from what 656.1 did (for example a different repoId source), trimming hides a real design difference. Mitigation: the 653.2 DoR compares item by item against 656.1's diff before trimming; any divergence becomes a question back to the planner.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Recommended option taken: finished, signed work ships; the unclaimed task absorbs the rebase and scope-trim at its DoR step. Operator may override via cli-decisions override.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1), pending operator morning review

summary: check-task-moved.sh auto-closes an umbrella task when a sub-task commit subject names it (AISDLC-656 closed by 656.1); file a fix task?

options.description: File a fix task now (exact-id match + open-children guard + regression test)
Keep skipping per push; file in the morning
Hot-patch the hook tonight

body:
## Problem
scripts/check-task-moved.sh matched "(AISDLC-656)" in 656.1's commit subjects and moved the umbrella AISDLC-656 to backlog/completed while 656.2 and 656.3 are open. alpha caught it, dropped the commit and pushed with the documented AI_SDLC_SKIP_TASK_MOVE=1 skip, disclosed in #1161. It will recur for every sub-task whose subject cites the umbrella id.

## Options
- **opt-a (recommended):** file a framework backlog task now via dispatch's follow-up filing authority (RFC-0051): the hook must match the exact task id (656.1, not 656 as a prefix) AND refuse to move any task whose children are still open; add a regression test with a 656/656.1 fixture. Pro: stops a silent audit-trail corruption. Con: one more open task tonight.
- **opt-b:** keep using the skip env var per push and file in the morning. Pro: nothing. Con: skip env vars as routine is a known anti-pattern (pre-push gate discipline).
- **opt-c:** hot-patch the hook tonight outside the pipeline. Con: unreviewed change to a gate script.

## Counter-argument
The operator may prefer umbrella auto-close when the LAST child completes; the task should state that as the desired behavior rather than "never move umbrellas".
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Recommended option taken; routine skip-env pushes are a known anti-pattern and the bug corrupts the task audit trail.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1), pending operator morning review

summary: AISDLC-666 executor loop skill: ship as signed with 3 MEDIUM security findings (counted major), or fix (1)(3) now and re-review?

options.description: Ship as signed; file follow-ups; disclose false doc line
Fix (1) and (3) + doc now; fresh 3-reviewer round (Opus security); hand over if epsilon stalls; file (2) as follow-up
Fix only the doc sentence and SAFE_NAME filter

body:
## Problem
Epsilon's 666 is signed locally (head 6cda3ff7, not pushed). Code and test approved; security (Opus) approved with 3 MEDIUM recorded as major in the leaf counts: (1) cli-dispatch complete does not verify the caller holds the claim and --worker overwrites workerId, while executor.md says it refuses, a false security statement; (2) hard rules are advisory prompt text, SendMessage/cli-decisions answer/task create reachable from executor sessions, suggested PreToolUse rule; (3) roster identity match takes the first pid in the ancestor chain with no status filter, so a stale reused pid can misattribute a session. Epsilon is rate-limited until ~Oct 6. 666 blocks 667.

## Prior art
- Standing rule (operator): critical/major findings BLOCK ship; minor/suggestion are filed. Mediums here are counted as major in the leaf, so they block.
- A false security statement in a shipped skill is worse than the missing check itself: operators act on the doc.
- DEC-0015 established handover from a committed head with a fresh reviewer spawn.

## Options
- **opt-a:** ship as signed, file follow-ups, call out the false line. Con: violates the major-blocks rule; ships a false claim.
- **opt-b (recommended):** fix (1) claim check in complete.ts + stop --worker overwriting workerId, (3) skip non-running roster entries, prefer nearest ancestor, verify process is claude, and correct the doc line; fresh three-reviewer round with Opus security; hand over to beta or alpha from 6cda3ff7 if epsilon stalls. (2) is architectural (new PreToolUse enforcement for role sessions) and is filed as a follow-up task, not fixed inline. Con: patch-id change, one more review round, maybe a handover.
- **opt-c:** fix only the doc sentence and the SAFE_NAME filter. Con: leaves (1) and (3) as real, known gaps in a trust-sensitive skill with a now-accurate doc saying so.

## Counter-argument
(1) exists identically in write-verdict today, so 666 adds no new capability; one could argue it is pre-existing and out of scope. But 666 is the skill that TELLS executors the check exists, and the fix is ~a dozen lines next to code 666 already touches.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Major-class findings block ship; the false doc claim makes opt-a unacceptable; (2) is architectural and goes to a follow-up task.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1), pending operator morning review

summary: AISDLC-673 review plan schema: ship as approved with 2 security MEDIUMs open (opt-a) or fix compare-revision scope + 3 small defects now and re-review (opt-b)?

options.description: Ship as approved; carry (1)(2) + run cap + TOCTOU as 675 requirements
Fix (1) base+HEAD only, the 3 defects, run cap, boundary tests, header; (2) hard requirement on 675; fresh round; sign

body:
## Problem
Gamma's rebased 673 head 8dba37eb is approved by all three reviewers (no critical/major) but carries two security MEDIUMs: (1) compare-probe revisions are only syntax-checked, so a plan can name any local ref (including the shared stash, which can hold untracked .env) and diff it into model context; (2) read/search/compare targets are not limited to git-tracked files. Plus three small real defects (SECURITY_CHECKS lookup throws on 'constructor'; buildFallbackPlan returns ok:true unvalidated; unsafe hunk id throws instead of ok:false), no cap on run probes, and three missing boundary tests. (1) changes delta's design record.

## Options
- **opt-a:** ship as-is; record (1), (2), run cap, TOCTOU as 675 requirements; decline the rest. Con: ships a plan schema whose compare probe can read arbitrary refs; DEC-0018 said mediums are not shipped open.
- **opt-b (recommended):** fix now: compare revisions restricted to the code-supplied merge-base SHA and HEAD only (intended semantics: RFC-0052's compare probe compares base against head and nothing else); Object.hasOwn lookup; fallback plan validated against the schema, fail-closed; unsafe hunk id -> ok:false; run-probe cap; the three boundary tests; validate.ts header reworded until (2) closes. (2) stays a HARD requirement on 675 (task text amended in #1162). Fresh three-reviewer round, then sign. Con: one more round on the critical path.

## Counter-argument
(1) is only exploitable by whoever authors the plan, which is the strong model under framework control, so one could call it theoretical. But plans are derived from untrusted diff content and the stash is shared across sessions; a confused-deputy path to .env is exactly what RFC-0043 exists to deny.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Consistent with DEC-0018: medium security findings do not ship open on a trust-sensitive path; base+HEAD-only is the intended compare semantics; (2) moves to 675 as a hard requirement.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1), pending operator morning review

summary: AISDLC-657.3: gitignoreCovers matches only the exact .ai-sdlc/artifacts line; fix now with git check-ignore, ship and follow up, or widen the text matcher?

options.description: Fix now with git check-ignore + text fallback + test; fresh round
Ship as signed; disclose; file follow-up
Widen the text matcher to three more patterns; fresh round

body:
## Problem
657.3 (PR #1163, head ea8a2c6c, signed, all three approved) adds a doctor check and an execute-time sentinel for ignoring .ai-sdlc/artifacts. gitignoreCovers matches only the exact line, so `artifacts/`, `.ai-sdlc/` and `.ai-sdlc/*` are missed. The doctor check warns falsely on this repository (root .gitignore has `artifacts/`) and execute can append a redundant sentinel block. Push is held anyway on the lease-push question.

## Options
- **opt-a (recommended):** use `git check-ignore` through adapters.runCommand with a text-match fallback, plus a test; fresh three-reviewer round. Pro: git is the authority on ignore semantics (negations, nested files, global excludes); costs no queue time while the lease hold stands. Con: one more round.
- **opt-b:** ship as signed, disclose, file a follow-up. Con: ships a known false positive in an adopter-facing doctor check on our own repo.
- **opt-c:** widen the text matcher to three more patterns. Con: still a fresh round, and still wrong for negations and global excludes.

## Counter-argument
A minor finding normally ships with a follow-up. Here the adopter-facing doctor output would be wrong on day one, and the fix is free in wall-clock terms.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Adopter-facing false positive on our own repo; git check-ignore is the authority; no queue cost during the lease hold.

summary: AISDLC-666: two doc sentences still claim more than the code does (inflight removal on iterate-needed; stale/reused pid matching); correct text, ship, or change behavior?

options.description: Correct both doc sentences, add two tests, fresh round
Ship as signed; disclose; file follow-ups
Make iterate-needed release inflight (behavior change)

body:
## Problem
666 is signed (patch-id 6b04d155), all three approved, DEC-0018 fix confirmed. Two new low/minor findings are the same class as the original false-doc MEDIUM: (1) docs say `complete` removes the task from inflight/ for every outcome, but iterate-needed keeps the inflight manifest; (2) executor.md says stale entries and reused pids do not match, but the code only rejects a reused pid whose process is not claude. Also: write-verdict still skips the claim-holder check (outside DEC-0018), and two test gaps. Blocks the 666 push and 667.

## Options
- **opt-a (recommended):** text-only: correct both sentences to the actual behavior, add the iterate-needed done/ test and a `--worker ''` refusal test, fresh three-reviewer round. Pro: a skill that executors act on says only true things; one round; 682 pushes first meanwhile. Con: one more round.
- **opt-b:** ship as signed with disclosure and follow-ups. Con: repeats the exact failure DEC-0018 was about.
- **opt-c:** change behavior so iterate-needed releases inflight. Con: changes RFC-0051 loop semantics (an executor is supposed to keep the slot while iterating); open-question class, not a review fix.

## Counter-argument
These are lows, and lows normally ship. But the precedent set last night is that a doc must not overstate a guard in a trust-sensitive skill, and the cost is one round with no queue impact.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Same class as DEC-0018; text fix plus tests; the write-verdict claim check is added to AISDLC-684 scope.

body: 685 is the urgent fix for the machine-overload root cause (Stop hook runs workspace coverage per turn-end per session and orphans workers). Scope item (4) role skip reuses hierarchy-role.js, which is only on 666's unpushed branch. Options: opt-a wait for 666 (delays the overload fix); opt-b stack 685 on 666 (not off main; rebase and patch-id churn); opt-c duplicate role detection in the hook (semantics may diverge); opt-d (recommended) drop the role skip from 685, keep the env-var skip, and carry the role skip as scope item 6 of AISDLC-684, which already depends on 666. Single-flight lock, process-group kill and per-package scope remove the overload on their own; the role skip is an optimization. Counter-argument: without the role skip every executor still runs one scoped coverage run per turn-end; single-flight bounds that to one at a time machine-wide.

rationale: Urgent fix must not wait on or stack onto 666; role skip is an optimization and moves to AISDLC-684 item 6.

summary: Patch-coverage gate counts main's newer commits as PR changes on behind-main PRs (two-dot diff base..head); blocks #1165 and every PR behind main

options.description: Fix the script to diff from the merge-base; regression test; new task AISDLC-686 in the implementing PR
Edit ci.yml to pass HEAD^1 and HEAD on the merge ref
Keep rebasing behind-main PRs

body: CI run 37137246710 on #1165 (682): AISDLC-662.1 fixed the coverage run to use the merge ref, but the gate step still calls check-pr-patch-coverage.mjs with --base <pull_request.base.sha> --head <head.sha>, and the script diffs base..head (two-dot), so files changed on main after the PR branched count as PR changes and fail with 'NO coverage data' although the true patch total is 87.8%. Options: opt-a (recommended) script diffs from git merge-base(base, head); scripts-only, regression test with a base tip ahead of the merge-base on untouched files. opt-b change ci.yml to pass HEAD^1/HEAD on the merge ref; workflow edit, operator-side. opt-c keep rebasing behind-main PRs; needs lease pushes and treats the symptom. Counter-argument: merge-base diff could hide a PR that reverts a main change; it cannot, since a revert is itself a PR change relative to the merge-base.
by: planner (Claude Fable 5.1, on behalf of dominique@reliablegenius.io)

rationale: Scripts-only root-cause fix; no workflow edit; unblocks every behind-main PR without lease pushes.
